title: How Well Do LLMs Simulate Survey Responses Following a Breast Cancer Screening Intervention?

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing LLM prediction errors (using Normalized Wasserstein Distance) against human ground-truth survey responses across different age subgroups (e.g., 35-39 years vs. 55-59 years) to measure performance disparities.

Measuring the discrepancy between LLM-simulated survey responses and human ground truth across different employment statuses (e.g., employed vs. never employed) and housing types (e.g., public HDB flats vs. private properties, acting as a proxy for socioeconomic status in Singapore).

Evaluating the accuracy of LLM predictions across different ethnic groups (Chinese, Indian, Malay, Others) and analyzing qualitative reasoning errors on culturally situated constructs (like cancer fatalism and perceived affordability) using topic modeling.
Calculating and comparing prediction errors between simulated and actual survey distributions across varying marital statuses (e.g., married, never married, divorced, widowed).
